final_diagnosis.root_cause: The ts-order-service Deployment in the train-ticket namespace has been scaled to 0 replicas, leaving the Order Service completely unavailable. Kubernetes events show a deliberate controller-initiated scale-down from 1 to 0 with a graceful pod termination, with no crash, OOM, or image-pull failures.
final_diagnosis.report:
The ts-order-service Deployment in the train-ticket namespace has been scaled to 0 replicas, leaving the Order Service completely unavailable

## Findings
• ts-order-service Deployment has 0 desired/available/ready replicas (0/0 0 0, age 6m2s) per list_eks_deployments.
• No ts-order-service-* pod exists in the namespace per list_eks_pods.
• get_eks_events shows Normal ScalingReplicaSet scaling ts-order-service-dd54d5df9 from 1 to 0 at ~4m56s ago.
• Pod ts-order-service-dd54d5df9-ljbb8 was deleted via SuccessfulDelete and the container was stopped via a Normal Killing event (graceful shutdown).
• No BackOff, OOMKilled, ImagePullBackOff, or CrashLoopBackOff events are present for ts-order-service.
• All other 42 ts-* deployments and infra deployments (rabbitmq, nacos, tsdb-mysql, nacosdb-mysql) are healthy and Ready.
• Worker nodes are functional; other pods are scheduling and reaching Ready across worker-01/02/03.

*Non-Validated Claims (Inferred):*
• The actor/source that set replicas to 0 (kubectl user, HPA with minReplicas=0, GitOps sync, chaos experiment, or operator) is unknown because DescribeResource, GetAppYAML, and GetServiceDependencies were unavailable.
• Whether an HPA or CronJob/Argo Rollouts/Chaos Mesh experiment triggered the scale-down.
• Exact downstream user-facing impact (booking, cancellation, payment flows) is inferred from typical Train-Ticket dependencies but not confirmed via traffic/error metrics.

## Recommended Actions
• Immediately restore replicas: kubectl -n train-ticket scale deployment/ts-order-service --replicas=1.
• Verify recovery: kubectl -n train-ticket rollout status deployment/ts-order-service and confirm a 2/2 Running pod (app + istio-proxy).
• Investigate cause: kubectl -n train-ticket describe deployment ts-order-service; inspect annotations, owner references, and last-applied-configuration.
• Check kubectl -n train-ticket get hpa for any HPA targeting ts-order-service with minReplicas=0 or broken metrics.
• Review GitOps (ArgoCD/Flux) history and audit logs for a recent commit/sync that set replicas: 0.
• Check chaos tooling (Chaos Mesh, Litmus) for experiments targeting ts-order-service.
• Smoke-test the booking flow through ts-gateway-service to confirm dependents (cancel, rebook, execute, preserve, inside-payment) are working.
• Add a guardrail alert when any ts-* deployment has spec.replicas==0 or availableReplicas<1 for >2 minutes.
• Document in the Train-Ticket runbook that ts-order-service is a critical single-replica service and must not be scaled to 0 outside of planned maintenance.


*Cited Evidence:*
- Queries: GetAlerts, list eks pods, list eks deployments, get eks events, DescribeResource, GetServiceDependencies, GetAppYAML


Timing: 88s
